l4_steps.name: Receive and log AD/SB notice into tracking system
l4_steps.input: FAA AD Federal Register notice or OEM Service Bulletin release
l4_steps.output: Applicability assessment report with fleet impact analysis
l4_steps.kpi: AD applicability assessment completed within 3 business days of issuance; 100% of ADs logged
l4_steps.pain_point: AD applicability across mixed fleet configurations (different mod states, AFMS revisions) requires manual cross-check in CAMP — no automated fleet-wide applicability filter exists, creating missed-applicability risk on large fleets

l4_steps.name: Assess compliance deadline and work priority flag
l4_steps.input: Applicability assessment report, AD/SB compliance timeframe, flight-hours and cycles data
l4_steps.output: Compliance deadline schedule, priority classification (EAD / mandatory / optional)
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of mandatory ADs scheduled before compliance deadline; 0% AD overrun rate
l4_steps.pain_point: Short-fuse Emergency ADs (EADs) compress planning windows to less than 48 hours, forcing AOG-level priority and displacing planned line maintenance events across multiple stations

l4_steps.name: Determine mandatory vs. optional modification track
l4_steps.input: AD/SB classification, compliance deadline, cost-benefit analysis for optional SBs
l4_steps.output: Work authorization decision: mandatory track (expedite) or optional track (standard planning)
l4_steps.kpi: Mandatory ADs never exceed compliance deadline — 0% regulatory non-compliance rate
l4_steps.pain_point: Optional SBs reclassified as mandatory mid-stream (e.g., OEM safety recommendation upgrade) force reprioritization and resource reallocation from already-scheduled maintenance events

l4_steps.name: Develop Engineering Order from OEM technical data
l4_steps.input: Approved SB/AD task data, AMM chapter reference, IPC part numbers
l4_steps.output: Engineering Order (EO) with task card, materials list, and tooling requirements
l4_steps.kpi: EO development cycle 5 business days for standard modifications; 2 days for emergency ADs
l4_steps.pain_point: Boeing TechConnect access latency and AMM revision currency issues cause engineers to reference outdated task data — no automated revision alert in AMOS when OEM documentation is superseded post-EO creation

l4_steps.name: Classify modification as major or minor alteration
l4_steps.system: FAA FSIMS (Flight Standards Information Management System)
l4_steps.input: Engineering Order draft, modification scope and system criticality assessment
l4_steps.output: Major/minor alteration determination per FAR Part 43 Appendix A; DER involvement decision
l4_steps.kpi: Major/minor determination documented within 1 business day of EO draft completion; 0% misclassification findings on FAA audits
l4_steps.pain_point: Major vs. minor alteration boundary under FAR Part 43 Appendix A is subjective for novel avionics integrations — misclassification exposes the airline to FAA enforcement action and certificate action during oversight audits

l4_steps.name: Submit Engineering Order to CAMO for formal approval
l4_steps.input: Completed EO with DER determination, SB copy, applicability data, materials list
l4_steps.output: CAMO-approved EO, released work order number in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: CAMO EO approval turnaround 2 business days for standard modifications; same-day for EADs
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS approval workflow does not enforce mandatory attachment validation (SB copy, applicability data), allowing incomplete EOs to route to the shop floor and cause mid-task holds for missing documentation

l4_steps.name: Raise parts requisition for avionics LRUs and consumables
l4_steps.input: Approved EO materials list, IPC part numbers, supplier approved vendor list (AVL)
l4_steps.output: Purchase order or stores issue request for LRUs, connectors, wire, and consumables
l4_steps.kpi: Parts availability confirmed 72 hours before scheduled modification slot; on-time parts availability rate 95%
l4_steps.pain_point: Avionics LRU lead times from OEM-approved suppliers (Honeywell, Collins Aerospace) can reach 60–90 days — long-range parts planning is rarely executed because modification scheduling is reactive, creating AOG parts shortages

l4_steps.name: Verify parts serviceability, traceability, and shelf-life
l4_steps.input: Parts received from stores or supplier, FAA Form 8130-3 / EASA Form 1 certificates
l4_steps.output: Go/No-Go decision for scheduled modification slot; quarantine order if parts rejected
l4_steps.kpi: Parts shortage-driven deferral rate 5% of avionics work orders; counterfeit parts detection — 0 unapproved parts reaching aircraft
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS parts provenance tracking does not automate FAA AC 21-29D traceability chain verification for avionics LRUs — manual document review required, and counterfeit avionics parts remain an active industry risk (FAA SUP-04 flag)

l4_steps.name: Reserve hangar bay, tooling, and technician staffing
l4_steps.input: Approved EO, parts availability confirmation, aircraft schedule and induction date
l4_steps.output: Confirmed maintenance event: hangar bay, specialized avionics tooling, staffing plan, and ground support equipment reservation
l4_steps.kpi: Avionics modification slot utilization 85%; aircraft out-of-service time within 10% of planned duration
l4_steps.pain_point: Avionics modifications requiring simultaneous avionics and airframe access create hangar bay scheduling conflicts, particularly when consolidated with heavy check inputs — bay and lift equipment contention causes schedule slippage

l4_steps.name: Remove existing avionics LRU and prepare installation zone
l4_steps.input: Approved EO task card, aircraft inducted into maintenance bay, tooling issued
l4_steps.output: Removed LRU tagged with part number, serial number, and removal date; cleared and inspected installation area
l4_steps.kpi: LRU removal and serviceable tagging completed per AMM procedure; 0 FOD events per modification event
l4_steps.pain_point: Trax task card completion tracking is not real-time on the hangar floor — supervisors rely on end-of-shift paper sign-offs that delay discrepancy identification and extend aircraft ground time

l4_steps.name: Install avionics modification per EO and AMM procedure
l4_steps.input: Approved EO, new LRU with FAA Form 8130-3, wiring diagram, torque specifications
l4_steps.output: Installed avionics component with completed installation task card; connector and harness photographs
l4_steps.kpi: Installation rework rate 2% of avionics work orders; first-time quality rate 98%
l4_steps.pain_point: Wire harness modifications on older aircraft encounter undocumented prior non-standard SB wiring deviations not reflected in current AMM diagrams — creates FOD risk and requires unplanned engineering investigation, extending aircraft down time

l4_steps.name: Inspect wiring integrity, bonding, and HIRF protection
l4_steps.input: Completed wiring installation, bonding resistance test results, HIRF test equipment readings
l4_steps.output: Wiring inspection pass/fail determination; rework order issued if failed
l4_steps.kpi: Wiring inspection pass rate 96% first pass; rework cycle 4 hours; 0 HIRF non-conformances at release
l4_steps.pain_point: HIRF and lightning protection bonding measurements require specialized test equipment not always available at line stations — deferred compliance testing creates a safety gap and requires ferry flight restrictions until verified

l4_steps.name: Load approved avionics software and update configuration data
l4_steps.input: Approved software part number, Loadable Software Aircraft Part (LSAP) list, aircraft data loader
l4_steps.output: Confirmed software load complete; post-load configuration report with part number and version verification
l4_steps.kpi: Software load completion without error within 2 hours; LSAP compatibility verified against aircraft CDS 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: LSAP version mismatches between aircraft Configuration Deviation Sheet (CDS) maintained in CAMP and the physical installed state cause rejected loads — manual CDS reconciliation is error-prone during high-tempo fleet-wide software campaigns

l4_steps.name: Execute functional ground test per approved test procedure
l4_steps.input: Completed modification, aircraft on ground power unit, approved test procedure and acceptance criteria
l4_steps.output: Functional test report with pass/fail for each test parameter; BITE fault code log
l4_steps.kpi: Avionics ground test pass rate 94% first run; 0 open safety-of-flight defects at release
l4_steps.pain_point: BITE test coverage on older avionics line-replaceable units may not fully exercise the modification scope — supplemental manual test procedures are required but not always linked in AMOS task cards, creating coverage gaps discovered only during flight test

l4_steps.name: Evaluate test results against acceptance criteria
l4_steps.input: Functional test report, BITE fault codes, acceptance criteria from EO and AMM
l4_steps.output: Airworthiness determination: proceed to release or raise defect work order for rework
l4_steps.kpi: Discrepancy rate at final test 4%; 0 open safety-of-flight items at time of release
l4_steps.pain_point: Test acceptance criteria for modified systems sometimes reference superseded test procedures — AMOS and Trax do not flag document revision status at time of test sign-off, allowing outdated acceptance limits to be applied to new configurations

l4_steps.name: Complete maintenance release and regulatory documentation
l4_steps.input: Completed task cards, functional test report, DER approval (if major alteration), FAA Form 8130-3
l4_steps.output: Signed maintenance release; FAA Form 337 filed for major alterations; updated aircraft log entry
l4_steps.kpi: Maintenance release documentation completeness 100% before aircraft release; FAA Form 337 filed within 30 days of major alteration completion
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA Form 337 filing for major alterations is a paper-plus-digital hybrid process in FAA FSIMS with no automated submission confirmation — missed or late filings are only discovered during FAA Principal Inspector audits, exposing the operator to civil penalty

l4_steps.name: Update aircraft configuration records and return to service
l4_steps.input: Signed maintenance release, EO closure, modification documentation package
l4_steps.output: Updated aircraft status in CAMP (mod state, AFMS revision, AD compliance record); aircraft released to operations
l4_steps.kpi: Configuration record update completed within 24 hours of maintenance release; CAMP mod state accuracy 99.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: CAMP Systems configuration record updates for multi-LRU modifications require manual entry of each modified item — bulk update capability is absent, creating data entry backlog during fleet-wide AD compliance campaigns and increasing the risk of mod state discrepancies between CAMP and physical aircraft
